newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's to open in 100th and 101st countries.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's to open in 100th and 101st countries.

text.p: McDonald's Corp. said Monday it was planning Big Mac attacks Tuesday on the chilly Belarussian capital of Minsk and tropical Tahiti's Papeete, where it will open fast-food restaurants in its 100th and 101st country or territory.
McDonald's also opened what it said was the world's first ski-through restaurant in the popular Swedish ski resort of Lindvallen about 280 miles northwest of Stockholm.
The world's largest restaurant chain, a symbol of American culture, established its first beachheads outside the 50 United States in Canada and Puerto Rico nearly three decades ago in 1967.

"With the openings of countries No. 100 and No. 101, McDonald's is present in nations accounting for about 75 percent of the world's population," McDonald's International President Jim Cantalupo said in a statement.
McDonald's said it operates more than 20,000 restaurants on six continents.
"Nearly half of McDonald's systemwide sales and more than half of the company's operating income come from outside the U.S.," Cantalupo said.
McDonald's will open three restaurants in Minsk, where it has invested more than $15 million. One outlet is planned for Tahiti.
In Eastern Europe, McDonald's operates 200 restaurants in 14 countries. "We're committed to continuing that growth in Eastern Europe," Cantalupo added.
McDonald's plans to spend $1 billion over the next three to four years opening restaurants in Eastern Europe, Cantalupo said in an interview.
Cantalupo also said it plans to open in 25 additional countries or territories in the next three or four years, including Ukraine and Pakistan next year.
McDonalds had originally said Monday it was opening in its 100th country, but later clarified its announcement.
"We take a little literary license, Cantalupo said. "We talk about countries and territories."
At the ski-through restaurant in Sweden, called "McSki," skiers can order hamburgers and French fries through a special window and ski off, munching as they go.
The restaurant, which also has indoor seating for about 140 people, is some 110 yards from the resort's main ski lift, which can carry about 3,000 people an hour.
McDonalds said it aimed to have 200 restaurants in Sweden by the year 2000, up from 120 today.
McDonald's shares rose $1.25 to $48.125 Monday on the New York Stock Exchange.
